# HProgress

> Native determinate or indeterminate progress, with percentage text and semantic colors.

[Start with the Hearth UI agent index](../../../llms.txt). This reference describes repository source; package.json version: 0.2.0. Match it to the source/release you are using.

## Identity

- Vue export: `HProgress` from `@samishal1998/hearth-ui`.
- Custom element: `<hearth-progress>`.
- Individual constructor: `HearthProgressElement` from `@samishal1998/hearth-ui/elements`.
- Category: Feedback.
- [Implementation](https://github.com/samishal1998/hearth-ui/blob/main/src/components/HProgress.vue).

## Choose and use it correctly

- value/max describe completed work. Omitting value, or setting indeterminate, creates an indeterminate progress indicator.
- The native progress element supplies progressbar semantics; do not add conflicting roles or fake percentages for unknown progress.
- Use HStatCard for a static metric and HSkeleton for loading content shapes.

## Public API

label, description: string · value, max: number · indeterminate, showValue: boolean · tone: Tone

A `?` marks optional source props. A prop with a default may be omitted even when the source type is required. Internal `formDisabled` and `control-sync` plumbing is excluded below; do not use it in application code.

```ts
type Props = {
    value?: number;
    max?: number;
    label?: string;
    description?: string;
    indeterminate?: boolean;
    tone?: Tone;
    showValue?: boolean;
};
```

### Defaults

```ts
{ max: 100, label: "Progress", tone: "accent", showValue: true }
```

### Events

None

Vue-emitted custom-element events expose arguments as `event.detail`, an array. Listen directly on the element. Native DOM events such as `click` keep their normal payloads.

### Slots

None

Vue uses `<template #slotName>`; custom elements use `<div slot="slotName">`. Custom elements do not support Vue scoped slots.

### CSS parts

base, label, value, track, description

Use `hearth-progress::part(part-name)` for an exposed part, or inherited `--h-*` tokens for system-level styling. Native Vue components use the shared stylesheet and `h-*` classes.

## Supporting types

```ts
export type Tone = "neutral" | "accent" | "success" | "warning" | "danger" | "info";
```

## Vue example

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { HProgress } from '@samishal1998/hearth-ui';
import '@samishal1998/hearth-ui/styles.css';

</script>

<template>
  <HProgress label="Discovery scan" :value="35" :max="100" />
  <HProgress label="Connecting" indeterminate />
</template>
```

## Web-component example

Provide a mount point (use a `form` instead of `div` when demonstrating field submission):

```html
<div id="example"></div>
```

The following is bundler-based ESM. For raw HTML, load `dist/themes.css` with a stylesheet link and import `registerElements` from `./dist/elements/index.js` instead. Set array/object properties before connection when they should become reset defaults.

```js
import { registerElements } from '@samishal1998/hearth-ui/elements';
import '@samishal1998/hearth-ui/themes.css';
registerElements();

const mount = document.querySelector('#example');
const element = document.createElement('hearth-progress');
Object.assign(element, {
  "label": "Discovery scan",
  "value": 35,
  "max": 100
});
mount.append(element);
```

## Related components

- [HSkeleton](../skeleton/llms.txt): Text, rectangle, and circular loading placeholders with reduced-motion support.
- [HStatCard](../stat-card/llms.txt): A quiet overview metric with tabular numbers, an icon, and a supporting label.
- [HAlert](../alert/llms.txt): Inline feedback for success, information, and problems. Errors announce as alerts; other tones use status.
